Fact.Name: AMT exemption amount (before phaseout)
Fact.Description: #77: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) §4.10, p. 16: "For taxable years beginning in 2026, the exemption amounts under § 55(d)(1) are: Joint Returns or Surviving Spouses $140,200; Unmarried Individuals (other than Surviving Spouses) $90,100; Married Individuals Filing Separate Returns $70,100". IRC §55(d)(1) https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55. Same figures on Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf line 5.

Fact.Name: AMT exemption phaseout threshold
Fact.Description: #77: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) §4.10, p. 17: "[Filing status / Threshold Phaseout Amount / Complete Phaseout Amount] Joint Returns or Surviving Spouses $1,000,000 [complete phaseout $1,280,400]; Unmarried Individuals (other than Surviving Spouses) $500,000 [$680,200]; Married Individuals Filing Separate Returns $500,000 [$640,200]". IRC §55(d)(2), (d)(4)(A)(ii)(I)-(II).

Fact.Name: AMT 28% rate breakpoint
Fact.Description: #77: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) §4.10, p. 16: "under § 55(b)(1), the excess taxable income above which the 28 percent tax rate applies is: Married Individuals Filing Separate Returns $122,250; All Other Taxpayers $244,500". IRC §55(b)(1)(A)(i), (b)(1)(C).

Fact.Name: AMT 28% rate offset
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 7: "Otherwise, multiply line 6 by 28% (0.28) and subtract $4,890 ($2,445 if married filing separately) from the result." ($4,890 = 2% x $244,500; $2,445 = 2% x $122,250.)

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 1a
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 1a: "Subtract Schedule 1-A (Form 1040), line 43, from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 14". Schedule 1-A line 43 is the enhanced deduction for seniors, which AMT does not allow; Schedule 1-A lines 15/27/36 stay deducted.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 1b
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 1b: "Subtract line 1a from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 11b (if less than zero, enter as a negative amount)". Form 1040 (2026 draft) line 11b = AGI (/agi).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2a
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 2a: "If filing Schedule A (Form 1040), enter the taxes from Schedule A, line 7; otherwise, enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 12e". IRC §56(b)(1)(A)(ii) (no deduction for taxes in §164(a)) and §56(b)(1)(E) (no standard deduction), https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/56. Schedule A line 7 = line 5e + line 6; this app supports only line 5e (line 6 other taxes = $0 in scope).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 4 AMTI
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 4: "Alternative minimum taxable income. Combine lines 1b through 3." Lines 2b-3 are $0 in scope: Schedule 1 line 1/8z refunds and NOLs are not supported; other adjustments and preferences (2c-2t, 3) block via /flowKnockoutAmtPreferenceItems. IRC §55(b)(2).

Fact.Name: AMT exemption phaseout reduction
Fact.Description: #77: IRC §55(d)(2) "The exemption amount of any taxpayer shall be reduced (but not below zero) by an amount equal to 25 percent of the amount by which the alternative minimum taxable income of the taxpayer exceeds" the threshold, with §55(d)(4)(A)(ii)(IV) (as amended by P.L. 119-21 §70107) "by substituting '50 percent' for '25 percent'", https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55. Consistent with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 p. 17 complete-phaseout amounts (threshold + 2 x exemption).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 5 exemption
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 5 (Exemption chart; "If line 4 is over the amount shown above for your filing status, see instructions") with the §55(d)(2)/(d)(4) 50% phaseout. MFS add-back above $640,200 and the §59(j) kiddie-tax limit are knockouts.

Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 6: "Subtract line 5 from line 4. If more than zero, go to line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-". IRC §55(b)(1)(B) taxable excess.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 uses Part III
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 7: "If you reported capital gain distributions directly on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 7a; you reported qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a; or you had a gain on both lines 15 and 16 of Schedule D (Form 1040) (as refigured for the AMT, if necessary), complete Part III". #86b: same trigger as the regular-tax QDCG worksheet (scheduleD3 /usesQdcgTaxWorksheet, worksheet line 4 more than $0), now that line 7a capital gain distributions are supported; line 13 takes worksheet line 4, which includes them through worksheet line 3. Part III is complete for every supported return. Instructions for Form 6251 (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, Part III, Lines 13, 14, and 15: when none of statements (1) a different AMT gain or loss, including "a different AMT capital loss carryover", (2) Form 1040 line 15 is zero, or (3) a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 12 code B-F applies, "Use the regular tax amounts to complete lines 13, 14, and 15." Statement (1) is a yes to the AMT adjustments question (/flowKnockoutAmtPreferenceItems); (3) has no input in this tool; under (2) only AMT QDCG worksheet lines 2-4 are needed, and they don't depend on line 1, so line 13 is still scheduleD3 /qdcgLine4. Line 14 (Schedule D line 19) and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet stop the return, so lines 35-37 are skipped. Form 2555 is not collected. Tested in dividends.test.ts (#86b Form 6251 Part III). IRC §55(b)(3).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 18
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 2, line 18: "If line 17 is $244,500 or less ($122,250 or less if married filing separately), multiply line 17 by 26% (0.26). Otherwise, multiply line 17 by 28% (0.28) and subtract $4,890 ($2,445 if married filing separately)". IRC §55(b)(3)(A). Whole dollars (#178): this amount is entered on the form, so it is rounded to the nearest dollar, half a dollar up. 26 CFR 301.6102-1(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/301.6102-1): "any amount required to be reported on such form shall be entered at the nearest whole dollar amount ... a fractional part of a dollar shall be disregarded unless it amounts to one-half dollar or more, in which case the amount ... shall be increased by $1" (IRC §6102(a)(2), https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6102). Form 1040 instr. (2025), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you do round to whole dollars, you must round all amounts." Every other amount on this return is whole dollars, so Part III is too; line 38 then adds the amounts as entered on lines 18, 31 and 34, and line 40 compares the entered lines 38 and 39.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 9 tentative minimum tax
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 9: "Tentative minimum tax. Subtract line 8 from line 7." Line 8 (AMT foreign tax credit) is $0: 1099-INT foreign tax knocks out (interest /flowKnockoutHasForeignTaxPaid), and 1099-DIV foreign tax knocks out whenever line 7 is more than $0 (dividends /flowKnockoutDividendForeignTaxPaid).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 10
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 10: "Add Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16 (minus any tax from Form 4972), and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 1z. Subtract from the result Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 1 ... If zero or less, enter -0-." Form 4972 and Form 8978 are not supported ($0). #86: Schedule 3 line 1 is the foreign tax credit without Form 1116 (schedule3 /sched3Line1); when it is more than $0 the return stops unless line 7 is $0 (dividends /flowKnockoutDividendForeignTaxPaid), so line 8 stays $0 on every supported return. IRC §55(c).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 must be attached
Fact.Description: #122: Instructions for Form 6251 (2025), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf p. 1, "Who Must File": "Attach Form 6251 to your return if any of the following statements are true. 1. Form 6251, line 7, is greater than line 10." Line 8 is $0 (foreign tax paid is a stop), so line 9 = line 7 and this is /amt (line 11) greater than $0. Items 2-4 (general business credit on Form 3800; Forms 8834, 8911, 8801; negative lines 2c-3) cannot apply in scope: those credits are not supported and lines 2c-3 block via /flowKnockoutAmtPreferenceItems. Used to include the 2026 draft Form 6251 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf) in the PDF.

Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft lines 2c-2t and 3 (e.g., line 2i "Exercise of incentive stock options", line 2g "Interest from specified private activity bonds exempt from the regular tax", line 2l depreciation, line 2e/2f NOLs) and line 8 AMT foreign tax credit. IRC §56, §57, §58.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: unsupported AMT items
Fact.Description: #77: yes to /hasAmtPreferenceItems. Form 6251 lines 2c-2t / 3 / 8 are not computed, so a yes blocks submission instead of under-reporting AMT.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: unanswered AMT adjustments when Form 6251 is required
Fact.Description: #89: Form 6251 is attached when /form6251Required. Instructions for Form 6251 (2025), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf p. 1, "Who Must File", item 1: "Form 6251, line 7, is greater than line 10." Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf PDF p. 2 (form p. 1), line 4: "Alternative minimum taxable income. Combine lines 1b through 3." Lines 2c through 3 are not computed. /flowKnockoutAmtPreferenceItems starts with IsComplete(/hasAmtPreferenceItems), so an unanswered question is complete false there and must not be treated as "no". This stop is true only when Form 6251 is required and that question is not a complete answer, so those lines are not printed as zero. A complete false still files. A complete true is /flowKnockoutAmtPreferenceItems. 26 U.S.C. 55(b)(2), 56, 57.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: MFS AMTI over $640,200
Fact.Description: #77: Form 6251 (2026) draft, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f6251--dft.pdf p. 1, line 4: "(If married filing separately and line 4 is more than $640,200, see instructions.)" IRC §55(d)(2) last sentence (MFS AMTI add-back) is not implemented. $640,200 = Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) p. 17 MFS complete phaseout amount.
